_about: The Find my fit quiz's own values per platform (the rest of its scoring comes from the published answers and cards). Served next to the page and loaded with the code's ?v= number, so score.js and these values always arrive together: run build\bump-version.ps1 after editing this file. ease: how easy it is to run without technical skills (0 needs a developer, 3 easiest). look: the design control it suits (template, visual = arrange pages yourself, pixel = every detail). largeCatalogue / smallShop / b2b: stores it suits (b2b: profiles that name selling to other businesses). storeOnly: only for selling. agency: a common choice for designers and agencies; agencyOnly: mostly sold through them. customFrontEnd: built to feed an app or any front end. devControl: built to be coded. kind: for business sites, which platforms suit each answer to "Which is closest to what you do?". members: paid memberships and newsletters built in. leaveWhy: a platform’s own reason in place of “Easy to move to another platform later”, backed by its card’s “If you leave” (Sanity’s card says the website’s code is already yours). addOnsMany / addOnsSome: the size of the plugin or app library, for "Will you add features as the site grows?". Many: WordPress (plugin directory), Drupal (about 55,000 modules), Shopify ("over 16,000 apps"). Some: Magento (about 3,700, third-party count), BigCommerce ("Over 1,200 apps"), HubSpot (1,000+), Wix (no published total; about 800 by third-party count). Fewer: Squarespace (about 55 extensions), Webflow ("300+ Apps"), Framer, Ghost, Duda, Sanity. notIdeal: a card's "Less suited if" lines that clearly match a quiz answer. "if" is the start of the line as it reads on the card (the persona test and every publish check it's still there); "when" is the matching answers (all keys, any listed value). A match rules the platform out unless nothing else fits; the rule reads only the answers, never the card text. Lines with no clear matching answer stay plain text, including Ghost's "several languages" (its languages answer already counts against it) and WordPress’s "no maintenance" (managed hosting covers it, and the hosting question already counts against it). domainDocs: the platform's own help page for connecting a domain (official docs only; none where the developer's host does it), linked from the first steps on a result. Checked 2026-10-30.

leaveWhy.sanity: You own the site code and can export all your content

squarespace.if: You have a large product catalogue

webflow.if: You run a large online store
You want simple drag-and-drop without design skills

You need a large content site

bigcommerce.if: You want the very simplest setup for a tiny shop

drupal.if: It's a small site with no developer

duda.if: You're building it yourself outside an agency
